title: Cells and Living Things Review Test
description: Review practice for cell evidence, structures, and systems.

questions.prompt: Which item is living according to cell theory?
questions.questionText: Which item is living according to cell theory?
options: a bacterium made of one cell
a water droplet with no cells
a grain of sand with no cells
a metal spring that moves
questions.correctAnswer: a bacterium made of one cell
questions.explanation: A bacterium is a living single-celled organism. The other choices do not provide evidence of cells.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of mitochondria in many cells?
questions.questionText: What is the main function of mitochondria in many cells?
options: help release usable energy from food molecules
store water outside the cell
make the cell wall rigid
block all materials from entering the cell
questions.correctAnswer: help release usable energy from food molecules
questions.explanation: Mitochondria help cells release usable energy from food molecules.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would best support the claim that a pond sample contains living organisms?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would best support the claim that a pond sample contains living organisms?
options: Microscope observations show cells moving and dividing.
The pond water is clear.
The sample is cold.
The sample contains tiny grains of sand.
questions.correctAnswer: Microscope observations show cells moving and dividing.
questions.explanation: Cells carrying out life processes are strong evidence that living organisms are present.

questions.prompt: Which model would best help explain how a cell functions as a system?
questions.questionText: Which model would best help explain how a cell functions as a system?
options: a labeled diagram showing cell parts and how their jobs connect
a list of rocks sorted by color
a map of highways in a city
a thermometer reading from one afternoon
questions.correctAnswer: a labeled diagram showing cell parts and how their jobs connect
questions.explanation: A model that shows cell parts and connected functions can explain the cell as an interacting system.

questions.prompt: A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria, and a cell membrane, but no cell wall or chloroplasts. What type of cell is it most likely?
questions.questionText: A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria, and a cell membrane, but no cell wall or chloroplasts. What type of cell is it most likely?
options: animal cell
plant cell
nonliving mineral
water molecule
questions.explanation: Animal cells have cell membranes and often have nuclei and mitochondria, but they do not have cell walls or chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Why is saying 'it moves' not enough evidence that something is living?
questions.questionText: Why is saying 'it moves' not enough evidence that something is living?
options: Nonliving things can move, so stronger evidence such as cells is needed.
Living things never move.
Only multicellular organisms can move.
Movement proves that something has chloroplasts.
questions.correctAnswer: Nonliving things can move, so stronger evidence such as cells is needed.
questions.explanation: Movement alone can happen in nonliving things. Evidence that the object is made of cells is stronger.

options: A unicellular organism has one cell; a multicellular organism has many cells.
A unicellular organism has many tissues; a multicellular organism has no cells.
Only multicellular organisms can be living.
Only unicellular organisms use energy.
questions.correctAnswer: A unicellular organism has one cell; a multicellular organism has many cells.
questions.explanation: Unicellular means one cell. Multicellular means many cells.

questions.prompt: Which question best focuses on the function of a cell structure?
questions.questionText: Which question best focuses on the function of a cell structure?
options: What job does the structure do for the cell?
What color is the drawing of the structure?
Who named the structure first?
How many letters are in the structure's name?
questions.correctAnswer: What job does the structure do for the cell?
questions.explanation: Function means what something does. Asking about the job of the structure focuses on function.

questions.prompt: A plant cell's chloroplasts are damaged. Which cell function would be affected most directly?
questions.questionText: A plant cell's chloroplasts are damaged. Which cell function would be affected most directly?
options: using light energy to make sugars
forming bones
hearing sounds
carrying oxygen through blood
questions.correctAnswer: using light energy to make sugars
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the structures that help many plant cells use light energy to make sugars.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why cells are studied with microscopes?
questions.questionText: Which statement best explains why cells are studied with microscopes?
options: Many cells are too small to see clearly with only our eyes.
Cells are always larger than organs.
Microscopes turn nonliving things into cells.
Microscopes show only the outside of large animals.
questions.correctAnswer: Many cells are too small to see clearly with only our eyes.
questions.explanation: Many cells are microscopic, so microscopes help scientists observe them.

questions.prompt: A student finds a sample that moves in water but has no visible cells after careful microscope observation. What should the student conclude?
questions.questionText: A student finds a sample that moves in water but has no visible cells after careful microscope observation. What should the student conclude?
options: Movement alone is not enough evidence; more cell evidence is needed.
Anything that moves is definitely alive.
The sample must be a plant cell.
Microscopes cannot help study living things.
questions.correctAnswer: Movement alone is not enough evidence; more cell evidence is needed.
questions.explanation: Some nonliving things can move. Cells are stronger evidence for life.

questions.prompt: Which pair best compares plant and animal cells?
questions.questionText: Which pair best compares plant and animal cells?
options: Both have membranes; plant cells often also have cell walls and chloroplasts.
Only animal cells have membranes.
Only plant cells use energy.
Both always have chloroplasts.
questions.correctAnswer: Both have membranes; plant cells often also have cell walls and chloroplasts.
questions.explanation: Plant and animal cells share some structures but differ in others.

questions.prompt: A model leaves out the cell membrane. Which function is hardest to explain with that missing part?
questions.questionText: A model leaves out the cell membrane. Which function is hardest to explain with that missing part?
options: how the cell controls what enters and leaves
how a plant cell wall gives support
how chloroplasts use light
how microscopes make objects look larger
questions.correctAnswer: how the cell controls what enters and leaves
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is the controlled boundary of the cell.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern best supports that a sample contains living cells?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern best supports that a sample contains living cells?
options: More cells are visible after time in a nutrient solution.
The sample's container is round.
The sample is stored near a window.
The sample makes no pattern under a microscope.
questions.correctAnswer: More cells are visible after time in a nutrient solution.
questions.explanation: An increase in visible cells in nutrients supports growth of living cells.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the strongest review summary?
questions.questionText: Which statement is the strongest review summary?
options: Living things are made of cells, and cell structures help cells perform needed functions.
All cells are identical in shape and job.
Cells matter only in plants.
The largest structure is always the most important one.
questions.correctAnswer: Living things are made of cells, and cell structures help cells perform needed functions.
questions.explanation: This summary connects the core evidence for life with structure and function.
